contract_root.statement: Let $A=\{1,2,4,8,13,21,31,45,66,81,97,\ldots\}$ be the greedy Sidon sequence: we begin with $1$ and iteratively include the next smallest integer that preserves the Sidon property (i.e. there are no non-trivial solutions to $a+b=c+d$). What is the order of growth of $A$? Is it true that\[\lvert A\cap \{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \gg N^{1/2-\epsilon}\]for all $\epsilon>0$ and large $N$?

composition_claim.text: Children 1–3 fix the greedy-Sidon convention (Sidon preservation, one distinct positive element per stage) and control each greedy step through the gap bound of child 4, which feeds a stage-wise recursion on the maximum; child 3 converts stages into the decidable count sidonCount N, and child 5 (the counting core derived from the gap recursion) gives |A∩[1,N]| ≥ c N^{1/2}/(log N)^K with constants depending only on the construction.
